title: Acts and the letters, looking back
hook: Lydia, Priscilla, Paul's chains, faith, hope, love
tomorrow: whose voice do you follow when everyone has advice?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Matthew: God with us on page one, with you alway in the last verse, read as comfort or as a promise for the road. The line was with you always.

An envelope in the mailbox with your name in someone's own handwriting. It lands differently than a text. The first churches in Acts didn't meet in church buildings. They met in houses, and they were held together by letters, read aloud and passed along. Some of those letters still carry a trace of the hands that wrote them.
screen: `YOUR NAME, IN SOMEONE'S HAND.` → `CHURCHES IN HOUSES.` → `HELD TOGETHER BY LETTERS.`

segments.voice: Start with a house. By a riverbank, Paul meets Lydia, "a seller of purple", "whose heart the Lord opened". She's baptized with her household and insists Paul's group stay at her home, and later the believers gather there. Paul greets two tentmakers, Priscilla and Aquila, who risked their necks for him, and adds, "Likewise greet the church that is in their house." A church, in a house. Now the paper. One to tell a friend tonight: at the end of Romans, the man holding the pen says hello. "I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord." Then, in Galatians, Paul takes the pen himself: "Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand." And Colossians closes with his signature and a request: "The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds." A man signing his name in chains. To a quarreling church in Corinth, he wrote the line that holds the rest: "And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity." In that chapter of the King James, charity means love, the kind that suffers long and is kind, not a donation. Faith keeps you going. Hope looks ahead. Love is what's still standing when the quarrel is over.
screen: `LYDIA'S HOUSE.` · `TERTIUS HOLDS THE PEN.` · `REMEMBER MY BONDS.` · `FAITH, HOPE, CHARITY.` · then, large: `THE GREATEST IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Find paper and a pen, and write a few lines by hand to someone who held you together on this road: a thank-you, a memory, one plain word of love. Feel the pen move, and let your handwriting be yours, crooked or not. You don't have to send it today.
Acts and the letters. A church in homes and riverbanks and prison cells, held together by paper, and by faith, hope and love.
Your line: the greatest is love. The King James calls it charity, the love that suffers long and is kind. Go gently.

howItsDone: Churches read Paul's letters aloud in worship, and 1 Corinthians 13, with faith, hope and love, is a reading some couples choose for their weddings.

fork.setup: a friend starts a Bible study with five people in her apartment. her cousin says it's not a "real" church. what does the text give her?
options: nothing: a church needs a building and a pastor first.
Paul greets 'the church that is in their house.'
only a Sunday-morning meeting counts as church.
fork.reveal: churches define 'a church' in different ways, but the letters greet whole churches meeting in homes, like Priscilla and Aquila's (Romans 16:5).

original.note: Greek: love. in 1 Corinthians 13:13 the King James gives it as charity.

trapdoor: what you thought: the early church was an institution with buildings and offices.
what it means: a web of houses, friends, letters and chains, held together by love.
what a scholar hears: the letters keep traces of their making: a scribe's greeting in Romans 16:22, and Paul's own hand in Galatians 6:11 and Colossians 4:18.
guess: the early church in homes, held together by Paul's letters
the laws Moses gave Israel, collected into one book
the stories of Jesus's childhood in Nazareth
recall: the Gospel that ends: with you always

chat.says: writing nia an actual letter. on paper. weird? i keep trying to fix her parents in it.
options: Not weird. Skip the fixing and write the love part: patient, kind. Paper is how Paul did it.
A little weird. Paper feels formal now; a long text would say the same thing faster.
Keep the fixing in. List reasons her parents might still get back together; hope helps.
chat.meaning: Paul's letters held whole house churches together, and his center is love that suffers long and is kind, not a solution.

Lydia.meaning: a seller of purple cloth who hosted the believers in her home

Priscilla.meaning: a tentmaker who, with Aquila, hosted a church in their house

Aquila.meaning: Priscilla's husband, a tentmaker who worked alongside Paul

Tertius.meaning: the man who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans

Corinth.meaning: a Greek city whose quarreling church got Paul's letters
